title: Synthetic demo: flow over a surface
attribution: Synthetic data generated by seismic_art (no real survey)
flow_note: flow follows steepest descent: toward increasing time

grid.row_note: row 0 is the southern edge; rows run north

critical_points.truth: pass between the two domes (80 m from their midpoint)

critical_note: high = local minimum of time (shallow; flow runs away), low = local maximum (deep; flow converges); relief = how far the time stands from the median of a ring of surroundings; value = mean attribute within the same radius; saddle = flat point with two deeper and two shallower lobes (relief = the weakest lobe), axis_deg = direction of the deeper lobes (counter-clockwise from east, 0-180)
notes: values are relative; compare within this file only
structure = picked time; the dip is the slope of a local plane fitted to the picks in a Gaussian window of 150 coordinate units, on a regular map grid of 12.5-unit cells (179 x 140)
dip is APPARENT: time change per map distance, not converted to depth
truth: two domes (shallow), one basin (deep), three amplitude anomalies (two on the dome crests, one off-structure)
names_note: surface names are illustrative: the synthetic layers are named after Norwegian North Sea units (Hordaland Gp, Balder Fm, Shetland Gp, Cromer Knoll Gp, Draupne Fm) in their stratigraphic order; they are not those formations, and their times, thicknesses and amplitudes are invented
